concept_summary: A reverse-loop game in the world of Threadline: a thread that bends only so many times: you begin holding everything the source hands out and win by giving it all back. Where the source loop is 'Draw and bend a thread with a fixed bend budget to route it past obstacles; each bend spends a shared resource.', here every move undoes the 'Draw and bend a thread with a fixed bend budget to route it past obstacles; each bend spends a shared resource.' loop step by step instead of advancing it, so the map empties and the score falls. Hoarding triggers the lose state; the end screen celebrates an empty board.
first_experiment: Paper prototype: ten tokens stand in for everything the player owns and each turn must discard at least one; test with five players whether emptying the board feels like winning after three rounds.
source_idea_title: Threadline: a thread that bends only so many times
why_it_is_opposite: While the source rewards accumulation (Draw and bend a thread with a fixed bend budget to route it past obstacles; each bend spends a shared resource.), this concept rewards the opposite: progress means having less, so a winning run here would score zero in the source.

concept_summary: The fantasy of Sonar: see with sound, but the dark listens back stretched over a single persistent season lasting months: one meaningful decision per evening, no grinding, no catching up. Progress compounds across real calendar time and a missed week bends the story instead of ending it. The finale is scheduled, shared, and unrepeatable.
first_experiment: Concierge test: run the core decision by hand over seven daily messages with three players; if day-seven return beats the source's second-session return, the long form has legs.
source_idea_title: Sonar: see with sound, but the dark listens back
why_it_is_opposite: While the source fits short sessions, this concept flips the clock: one season here outlasts hundreds of source sessions, so the source habit of quick payoff actively hurts.

concept_summary: The same core loop as COO: a 250-square-mile city built for a spy pigeon, rebuilt end to end for newcomers instead of its current crowd. Controls, difficulty, session shape, and rewards assume newcomers: a guided, jargon-free on-ramp for total beginners. Nothing in this build serves the old crowd; one client cannot satisfy both.
first_experiment: Take one level from the source fantasy, apply the inverted tuning only, and playtest with five target players for ten minutes; a quit-rate on the opposite side of half from the source baseline confirms the audience split is real.
source_idea_title: COO: a 250-square-mile city built for a spy pigeon
why_it_is_opposite: While the source is tuned for its current crowd (Players who want console-scale novelty without an install: systems tuned for veterans of the genre), this concept flips every tuning decision toward newcomers (a guided, jargon-free on-ramp for total beginners), so the two builds want mutually exclusive players.
